key_insight: AI for semen analysis is moving from single-task image recognition toward multimodal, clinically translatable systems that can support sperm detection, motility, morphology, and genetic integrity assessment.
clinical_relevance: If validated well, these tools could make semen evaluation more objective, reproducible, and scalable for infertility diagnosis and assisted reproductive technology workflows.
method: Computer vision and deep learning for sperm detection, counting, segmentation, and classification
Tracking-based analysis of motility from time-lapse microscopy videos
Multimodal fusion of images, videos, CASA outputs, DNA integrity assays, and clinical metadata
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes public datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation metrics, and emphasizes that performance must be tested beyond single-center retrospective results.
watch_item: Cross-center domain shift, inconsistent annotations, and limited prospective validation remain major barriers to safe clinical deployment.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Semen Analysis in Male Infertility: Computer Vision, Multimodal Fusion, and Clinical Translation
